intro: You are high on Mount Nemrut, on the East Terrace, at 2,150 metres. It is the second half of the 1st century BC, and King Antiochus I of Commagene has built his tomb-sanctuary here. At the foot of a gravel tumulus, gods eight to nine metres tall sit enthroned in a row: the king himself, Commagene, Zeus, Apollo and Herakles. An eagle and a lion guard either end, and a stepped altar faces them. In the model, the heads are back on their shoulders.
spot-1: Now you are looking at Zeus-Oromasdes, in the middle of the row, measured at 8.75 metres. He is two gods in one: Greek Zeus and Persian Ahura Mazda, joined in a single figure.
spot-2: Now you are looking at Antiochus I. Notice where he sits: not below the gods, but among them, and at exactly their height. A king who placed himself in divine company.
spot-3: Now you are looking at Herakles-Artagnes-Ares, the god at the right end of the row. Let your eye travel a little further: beyond him wait the eagle and the lion.
spot-4: Now you are looking at the lion. Together with an eagle, a lion closes each end of the row, like guardians standing watch over the enthroned gods.
spot-5: Now you are looking at the stepped altar. It stands at the east end of the court, facing the gods: the fire altar, where the sanctuary's rites were turned towards the seated figures.
spot-6: Now you are looking at the place of the ancestor stelae. Along both sides of the court they once stood in line: stelae of the king's Persian and Macedonian ancestors, two lineages framing a single court.
spot-7: Now you are looking at the tumulus, a gravel mound forty-nine metres high. Somewhere inside, perhaps, lies the king. Yet the burial chamber has never been found, and the mountain still keeps its secret.
uncertainty: Finally, a word about what this model does not know. The height and diameter of the tumulus come from the English Wikipedia; the court dimensions, the height of Zeus, the throne bases and the order of the figures from the German one. Only Zeus is measured, so all five colossi are drawn at his scale, which is why the bare-headed Herakles stands lower than the others. The seat height of the thrones (3 m), the 4.75 m of the eagle and the lion (the source says 4.5-5 m), the altar steps and the ancestor stelae are drawn by proportion. Today the statues stand headless, their heads on the ground before them; the model shows the sanctuary as built, heads in place, and the faces and tiaras are not copies of the originals. The lions are a scan of a seated marble lion from Delos, and the eagles a scan of a 16th-century marble eagle, both given the terrace's limestone: only fragments of Nemrut's own lions and eagles survive, and they were carved in Commagene's own style. The west and north terraces are not modelled.
